text: You ask an AI assistant a question your business should own, and it recommends someone else. The natural reaction is to build a theory on the spot about their pages, their domain or some clever trick. Theories like that are quick to form and costly to act on: a team can spend a quarter chasing a reason that turns out not to exist. This note is about a different habit: keeping a dated, question-by-question record of who gets named, and refusing to guess at motives.
